name: Solar disinfection (SODIS)
summary: Clear water in a clear PET bottle, laid in full sun for six hours, comes out biologically much safer — the method for when there is no fuel.
time: 6 hours of strong sun, or 2 consecutive days if overcast

materials.item: clear PET plastic bottle up to 2 litres
dark or reflective surface to lay it on

steps.text: Pre-filter or settle the water until you can read text through the full bottle.
steps.why: UV has to reach the organism. Turbidity shades it, and above about 30 NTU the method stops working.

steps.text: Fill the bottle three-quarters, shake it hard for 20 seconds to oxygenate, then top it up and cap it.
steps.why: Dissolved oxygen drives the photo-oxidative half of the kill, alongside the UV-A itself.

steps.text: Lay the bottle ON ITS SIDE in full sun — on a dark or metal surface if you have one — for at least 6 hours.
In overcast weather give it two consecutive days. If it has rained all day, the dose is not there.
Drink from the bottle it was treated in.

verify: You can read printed text through the filled bottle before you start — that is the turbidity check.
The bottle has had 6 hours of genuinely direct sun, not 6 hours of daylight in shade.
limits: SODIS greatly reduces bacteria, viruses and protozoa. It is a field-grade reduction, not a sterilization, and its dose depends on weather you do not control.
It removes nothing chemical or dissolved.
It fails on turbid water, in deep shade, and through glass windows or coloured/scratched bottles that block UV-A.
cautions: Use PET (drink bottles), not PVC. Scratched or cloudy bottles pass less UV and should be replaced.
Boiling is better whenever you have fuel. This is the fallback.
